question: Will a second televised debate between Taipei mayoral candidates Chiang Wan-an and Puma Shen be scheduled by November 13, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Base rate: Taiwanese mayoral races where the leading incumbent agreed to one debate rarely add a second; Chiang's camp has said 'coordinate' since mid-Oct without result. Update toward YES: on Nov 3 Chiang publicly said he 'tends to participate' if time/format are settled, campaign managers Wu Ssu-yao and Lo Chih-chiang exchanged LINE contacts, and a 10-outlet group is inviting both. Against: only ~10 days left, no negotiation meeting convened, Lo blames the media group for not approaching them, and the incentive of a market-favored incumbent (Polymarket ~61%) is to run out the clock. Campaign period and CEC policy presentations start Nov 13. No market found for this exact contract; only who-wins-Taipei markets on Polymarket, used just as a sign of Chiang's lead.
calls.dossier:
- Oct 31 2026: first Chiang-Shen TV debate (TVBS/SET). Shen invited Chiang to a second debate on air; Chiang said he was 'open' and that if invited, details would be coordinated (Focus Taiwan 2026-10-31; China Times 2026-10-31).
- Oct 31 2026: ten media outlets (Liberty Times, CTV, TTV, FTV, Mirror TV, CTS, ETtoday, EBC, Era/壹電視) issued a joint statement inviting both camps to a second debate. They proposed no dates and asked the campaigns to name negotiators soon (China Times 2026-10-31).
- Nov 2 2026: Chiang said the second debate is 'left to team coordination'. Shen wants an immediate-answer format for media questions (CNA 2026-11-02).
- Nov 2 2026: campaign managers Wu Ssu-yao (Shen) and Lo Chih-chiang (Chiang) exchanged LINE contacts to discuss a second debate. Lo publicly mocked Shen's camp, saying it should draft 'Shen-centered rules' first. No substantive talks reported (ETtoday 2026-11-02; FTV 2026-11-02).
- Lo claimed the media group, especially Liberty Times, had not contacted Chiang's team since businessman Robert Tsao told Shen not to debate (LTN search snippet, ~Nov 2-3).
- Nov 3 2026: in an interview with Shen Chun-hua, Chiang said 'I tend to participate, as long as time and format are settled'. He was pressed after repeatedly saying 'coordinate' (LTN 2026-11-03; NextApple 2026-11-03).
- Earlier history: Chiang said Oct 12 that he had 'no time' for a second debate, said on Oct 13 a second debate was possible after the first, and has said he is awaiting the invitation since Oct 15. Joint media invitations came Oct 12 (6 outlets), Oct 16 (8) and Oct 19 (10); no second date resulted.
- Status quo: as of Nov 3 there is no agreed or announced date for a second debate and no reported negotiation meeting.
- Calendar: CEC announces the candidate list Nov 12; the official campaign period and CEC policy presentations run Nov 13-27; the polling blackout starts Nov 18; election Nov 28.
- Base-rate note: recent Taipei mayoral races (e.g. 2018, 2022) are generally recalled as having one main televised debate. This is from memory, not a verified count. Leading candidates typically resist extra debates.
- Resolution instrument: resolves on a publicly announced specific date agreed by both campaigns or confirmed by the host with both participating (CNA topic page or credible sources). Willingness statements do not count.
- Event window: now -> 2026-11-13 23:59 Taipei time. As of 2026-11-03 13:20 UTC, roughly 10.4 days remain. The question opened around Oct 30, so roughly 30% of a ~14-day window has elapsed.
- Markets: no market on this specific question was found; only Polymarket markets on who wins Taipei exist.
- Searched but not found: any proposed date from the ten-outlet group, any scheduled negotiation meeting, any statement by TVBS/SET about hosting a second debate.
calls.reference_class: Taiwan major-city mayoral races in which the leading candidate accepted only one televised debate and was then asked for a second late in the campaign

calls.reasoning: Taipei mayoral races usually get one televised debate, and incumbents leading in the polls usually avoid a second. As of Nov 3 there is no host, date, format or coordination meeting; Chiang's camp says it is waiting for the 10-outlet media group. Pointing up: on Nov 3 Chiang said he was 'inclined to participate' once timing and format are agreed, the campaign managers have exchanged LINE contacts, and the first debate went from announcement to date in 4 days. Pointing down: Chiang leads 46-42 but lost the post-debate performance poll 47-40, so he has a reason to stall; his campaign manager mocks the rematch push; about 10 days remain. No matching prediction market found (Polymarket only prices the election winner).
calls.dossier:
- Oct 31 2026: first TVBS/SET debate held. The same day, 10 outlets (Liberty Times, CTV, TTV, FTV, CTS, Mirror TV, ETtoday, EBC, Era/Nian Dai) jointly invited both camps to a second debate and asked them to name negotiators for time, venue, rules and broadcast (LTN 5625020; Chinatimes 20261031).
- Earlier joint invitations: 6 outlets Oct 12, 8 outlets Oct 16, 10 outlets Oct 19 (question background).
- Oct 15: Chiang campaign manager Lo Chih-chiang said Chiang had already agreed to the second-alliance debate and was waiting for its coordination notice; he told DPP's Wu Ssu-yao that 'the earth doesn't revolve around' Shen (NOWnews 6883792).
- Nov 1-2: campaign managers Wu Ssu-yao (Shen) and Lo Chih-chiang (Chiang) exchanged LINE contacts to discuss the next debate. Lo mocked Shen with a sarcastic list of 'Shen-version rules' (e.g., unlimited rematches if he loses) and said the KMT is waiting for a formal coordination invitation from outlets such as Liberty Times (TVBS 4044736, Nov 2).
- Nov 2 CNA: Chiang says a second debate is 'for the team to coordinate.'
- Nov 3 CNA/UDN/NextApple: on Shen Chun-hua's show, after repeated pressing, Chiang said 'I'm inclined to participate' if the timing, details and format are agreed; he also said Shen 'didn't make good use' of the first debate. No date, host or meeting scheduled.
- TVBS post-debate poll: 47% thought Shen performed better vs 40% for Chiang; among likely voters Chiang 46%, Shen 42% (LTN 5625314).
- Precedent: the first debate went from host announcement (Oct 11) to a fixed date (Oct 15) in 4 days over two negotiation rounds. Taipei 2018 and 2022 each had a single televised debate.
- Calendar: official campaign period and CEC policy presentations Nov 13-27; poll blackout from Nov 18; election Nov 28.
- Markets: only Polymarket election-winner markets exist, no debate-scheduling market.
- Resolution: resolves off a date reported as agreed by both campaigns or confirmed by the host with both participating (CNA topic page or credible media), not off one side's proposal or 'inclined' statements.
- Event window: now -> Nov 13 2026 23:59 Taipei; as of Nov 3, roughly 68% of the time since the Oct 31 invitation has elapsed (~10.4 days remain).
- Searched for but not found: any scheduled coordination meeting from the 10-outlet group, any proposed dates after Oct 31, any formal written reply from Chiang's camp.
calls.reference_class: Taiwan metropolitan mayoral races where the frontrunner was publicly pressed for a second televised debate (Taipei 2018, 2022 each had one debate)

calls.reasoning: Status quo: no date as of Nov 3; ~10 days remain. On Nov 3 Chiang said he is 'inclined to participate' if format and time are agreed. His campaign (Lo Chih-chiang) says it is waiting for the 10-outlet alliance led by the Liberty Times to send a negotiation invitation, and the two campaign managers have added each other on LINE. Shen is eager. First debate: hosts announced Oct 11 and the date was fixed Oct 15, so a date can be locked within days once talks begin. Against: Chiang leads in the polls and has repeatedly stalled with 'waiting for the invitation' even though invitations went out Oct 12, 16 and 19. Taipei front-runners usually do one debate (background, not checked this run). Format disputes are likely, and the date could be fixed after Nov 13. No matching market found; Polymarket only prices the election winner (Chiang 0.61).

calls.reasoning: Status quo is NO: as of Nov 3 there is no host, date, format or coordination meeting, and Taipei races customarily have one televised debate, with leading incumbents resisting more. Upward: on Nov 3 Chiang said for the first time that he is 'inclined to participate', the campaign managers exchanged LINE contacts, a 10-outlet group is inviting both, and the first debate was fixed within 4 days once talks began. A second debate would land Nov 14-22, so its date would likely be announced before Nov 13. Downward: Chiang leads the polls but lost the performance poll, his camp has said 'waiting for the invitation' since mid-October, Lo mocks the rematch push, format disputes are likely, and only ~10 days remain.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs report the same facts: the Oct 31 ten-outlet invitation, the Nov 2 LINE contact exchange, Chiang's Nov 3 'inclined to participate' statement, no meeting or date as of Nov 3, and the Nov 13 start of the campaign period. Their differences (0.26-0.34) are judgment about how much the Nov 3 softening outweighs Chiang's front-runner incentive to stall. Lo's claim that the Liberty Times group has not contacted Chiang's camp could not be verified without web access. I weigh the repeated 'waiting for the invitation' pattern since mid-October as meaningful evidence of stalling, partly offset by the public cost of the Nov 3 statement and the short time needed to fix a date once talks start.
